title: Rate-window drift in multi-shard streaming attribution causing duplicated token billing
creator: Emily Park
description: Customer X reported a ~18% unexpected increase in billed token usage for a set of long-lived streaming sessions over the past 7 days. Investigation shows sporadic duplicated token attributions at the billing-aggregation layer for streaming connections that traverse multiple metering shards after LB session handoffs.
reproduction_steps: Simulate long-lived streaming session emitting small token deltas (avg 10 tokens every 30s) for 12+ hours.
Force LB (ingress) connection migration across two metering shards by toggling the instance pool weight during the session.
Observe per-shard event streams and aggregated billing events for duplicated token counts around the handoff moment.
logs_samples: ingress: session_id=abc123, client_fingerprint=fv9, shard=A, seq=1024, tokens=9, frame_id=4821
ingress: session_id=abc123, client_fingerprint=fv9, shard=B, seq=1, tokens=9, frame_id=4821 (after handoff)
investigation_summary: Root cause: a timing window mismatch between per-shard sliding-window deduplication (used by live rate limiter/quotas) and the billing aggregation job. When a streaming session is handed off between ingress shards (LB-induced), the incoming shard can replay the same frame/frame_id because session metadata (session_id) is rotated by the LB. The per-shard dedupe uses frame_id+shard as a key; the billing aggregator dedupes on frame_id only but runs with a slightly shifted rollup boundary (15s vs 10s) causing both shard events to survive de-duplication and be summed into daily billed tokens. Secondary factor: small keepalive frames lack a persistent idempotency token in the streaming frame which would have prevented attribution duplication.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix: change billing aggregator to dedupe using client_fingerprint+frame_id in addition to frame_id alone (deployed 2026-03-11).
Short-term: add an ingest-layer guard to drop frames with identical frame_id seen within 60s for the same session fingerprint (deployed 2026-03-12).
Medium-term: add idempotency_token to streaming frames and require LB to preserve session_id across handoffs (design approved).

2026-03-11: Initial engineering findings shared; engineering requested packet captures for 3 sample sessions.
2026-03-13: Explained root cause and action plan; promised refund calculation by 2026-03-15.
2026-03-14: Informed customer that an automated aggregation fix is live and that preliminary credits will be issued pending final reconciliation.
credits_issued: provisional credit of $14,350 (covers duplicated tokens from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); final reconciliation scheduled 2026-03-18
impact_analysis: Number of affected customers: 3 enterprise tenants using long-lived streaming (estimated).
Total overbilled tokens (preliminary): ~1.2M tokens across affected tenants over the week window.
% of daily billing spike for Customer X: ~18% on peak days.
timeline: 2026-03-09: Escalation filed by Support from Customer X
2026-03-11: Aggregator dedupe configuration hotfix rolled out (canary then global)
2026-03-13: Additional logging added to streaming frames for forensic capture
postmortem_actions: Revise deduplication contract between metering shards and billing aggregator (update docs + interface spec).
Require preserving session_id or LB-supplied stable_session_token for streaming handoffs (platform change ticket PM-412).
Introduce daily automated reconciliation job that detects rare duplicate-attribution patterns and flags for human review.
Add quota/test harness to simulate LB handoffs across shards and validate billing invariants (integration test).
follow_up_tasks: ENG-20390: Implement persistent idempotency_token for streaming frames and roll out SDK/ingress changes.
ENG-20410: Extend aggregation job to run a secondary dedupe pass using client_fingerprint.
PM-412: Coordinate with LB/platform to guarantee session preservation policy during connection migrations.
OPS-221: Run reconciliation + issue final credits by 2026-03-18
notes: This ticket is intentionally separated from ENG-19812 (retry amplification) — different root cause and fix set.
Billing team to review credit policy for multi-tenant cases where duplication stems from LB misconfigurations vs platform bug.
Schedule post-release review in Cycle 42 to validate that similar patterns do not reoccur under increased LB churn.
